topics.topic: Imported data-provider constant for the temporary-file mode
questions: The temporary-file creation mode must become a data-provider constant named in the passage as `the imported X constant`.
The literal temporary-file mode must become an imported data-provider constant named in the required form, or remain a design fact outside the generated specification.
The literal temporary-file mode must become a data-provider constant named in the passage as an imported constant, with that constant added to the decided policy values.

quotes:
The temporary name begins with the imported `TEMPORARY_NAME_PREFIX` constant and is chosen fresh for each
   write; the temporary file is created exclusively, never reusing an existing entry, with mode 0600 and
   takes its final mode before the rename.
judgement.why: The generated writer reads a fixed policy mode expressed as a literal rather than through an imported data-provider constant.

topics.topic: Required imported constant wording for record and store/state folder modes
questions: The passage must name `RECORD_MODE`, `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` and `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` as imported constants.
Each constant must be named as the imported `RECORD_MODE`, `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` or `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constant.
The passage must name `RECORD_MODE` as `the imported RECORD_MODE constant`.
The passage must name these values as `the imported STORE_FOLDER_MODE constant` and `the imported STATE_FOLDER_MODE constant`.

quotes:
A stored image has the mode of the imported `STORED_IMAGE_MODE` constant and a state record that of
   `RECORD_MODE`, so neither is executable. A folder the service creates in the binary store has the mode
   of `STORE_FOLDER_MODE`, and one in the state folder that of `STATE_FOLDER_MODE`.
judgement.why: RECORD_MODE, STORE_FOLDER_MODE and STATE_FOLDER_MODE are data-provider constants used by generated code but are not named in the required imported-constant form.

topics.topic: Runtime and native-codec boundary for deterministic JPEG bytes
questions: Does this require identical JPEG bytes only on repeated runs in one installed runtime, or across every installation that has the same image-library version, including different native codec builds and platforms?

Does “one library version” include and pin the native JPEG codec, its build options and every other encoder dependency that can affect the bytes, or must the claim be weakened to one fully fixed runtime installation?
What exactly belongs to the versioned determinism boundary: only the image-library package, or also its native JPEG codec, build options, platform and architecture?

quotes: With one library version one source gives the same bytes.
judgement.why: The rule states the determinism boundary as one library version rather than one installed runtime.

topics.topic: Temporary-name generation and collision handling during exclusive creation
questions: When exclusive creation finds that the chosen temporary name already exists, must the writer choose another name and retry, or fail the operation?
What must happen when exclusive creation finds that the chosen temporary name already exists, including a temporary entry left by a crash?
How is a fresh temporary name obtained, and what must happen when exclusive creation finds an existing entry with the chosen name?

quotes:
The temporary name begins with the imported `TEMPORARY_NAME_PREFIX` constant and is chosen fresh for each
   write; the temporary file is created exclusively, never reusing an existing entry, with mode 0600 and
   takes its final mode before the rename.

A write
   that fails before the rename leaves the destination as it was, whether absent or holding an earlier
   complete file, and removes its temporary file.

A crash of the process or the
   host is not a failed write: the temporary file it interrupts stays under its temporary name, is never
   read, and the service does not remove it.
judgement.divergence: One implementation retries exclusive creation with another name and completes the write; another treats the collision as a failed write, which the calling flow notices as failure instead of success.
judgement.why: The text requires exclusive fresh names but does not decide whether an occupied candidate triggers another selection or ends the write.

witness.initial: A process or host crash has left a temporary entry in the destination folder.
events: The calling flow requests a delivery whose writer selects the occupied temporary name.
The writer's exclusive creation reports that the entry already exists.
outcomes: The writer selects another temporary name and the delivery completes.
The writer treats exclusive creation as a failed write and the delivery fails.

questions: The decided `optimize`, `progressive` and `subsampling` values must be supplied through data-provider constants named as imported constants, or the passage must instead name one emitted backend symbol that owns the complete encoding recipe.
The fixed JPEG policy values must become imported data-provider constants named in the required form, or remain design facts outside the generated specification.

judgement.why: The fixed optimize, progressive and subsampling policy values are read by generated code but are supplied as literals rather than through one of the permitted value paths.

topics.topic: Outcome when post-decode image preparation or JPEG encoding fails
questions: What outcome applies when decoding succeeds but `ImageOps.exif_transpose`, conversion, thumbnailing, compositing or JPEG encoding fails?
What outcome is required when decoding succeeds but orientation, conversion, resizing, alpha compositing or JPEG encoding raises an error?

quotes: `Rejected` with `too_many_pixels`, `unreadable_image` or `too_large`.
judgement.why: The later prepare_photo contract closes its error outcomes to those three failures, so an image-library preparation or encoding error cannot become another refusal or an exposed server error.

topics.topic: Required INV-13 test coverage for clock-reading boundaries and replayed marks
questions: Which mark paths must the Required tests exercise to show the rule's zero-or-one reading boundary, including refusals before the clock point, refusals after it, and replayed marks?

Must the witness test also show the required clock counts for a mark refused before the reading point, a mark refused after it and a replayed mark, or is one successful mark sufficient to witness INV-13?

quotes: - INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged Required-tests coverage question previously judged in P6.

precedent.topic: Required clock-call coverage for every refused, replayed, and lock-refused mark outcome
quotes: - INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
precedent.why: The Required tests passage is unchanged from the closed text, and the formatting change to A7 rule 3 did not make its omission of separate refused and replayed mark cases matter.

topics.topic: Durability and failure handling for newly created folders
questions: Must creation of a binary-store or state folder be made durable by synchronising the new folder and its parent, and how does a failure of either synchronisation affect the operation?

quotes:
A folder the service creates in the binary store has the mode
   of `STORE_FOLDER_MODE`, and one in the state folder that of `STATE_FOLDER_MODE`.

Each file is written to a temporary name in its folder, synchronised to disk and renamed, and
   its folder is synchronised, so a reader sees a complete file or none. Atomicity is per file.

A stored image is written before a record that depends
   on it, so a failure to synchronise its folder after the rename fails that write: the image stays, no
   record is written, and A3 rule 5 condition 5 applies.

A placement or mark record is the last write of
   its operation, so a failure to synchronise its folder after the rename does not undo it and is not a
   failure of the operation; only its survival of a host crash is uncertain.
judgement.divergence: One implementation synchronises a newly created folder and its parent and reports a synchronization failure according to the file being written; another synchronises only the folder containing the file and may acknowledge state whose new directory entry is lost, which the caller and Portal notice after a crash.
judgement.why: The rules decide file and containing-folder synchronization but do not decide durability or synchronization-failure handling for a newly created folder's entry in its parent.

events: The calling flow requests a delivery.
The service creates the required folder, writes the image and placement record, and reaches the point where it could report success.
The host crashes immediately after the response.
outcomes: The implementation synchronised the new directory entry in its parent, so the acknowledged placement and stored image survive.
The implementation did not synchronise the parent, so the new folder and acknowledged placement may be absent after restart.
witness.observer: The calling flow after restart and the Portal when it reads the stored reference.

topics.topic: Response and write guarantees when the clock read fails
questions: What response and write guarantees apply if `utc_now` cannot return a current time at that reading point?

quotes:
Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken.
judgement.why: P8 already judged the same question about utc_now failing or violating its value contract, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Mark behavior when utc_now fails or violates its value contract
quotes: The current time in UTC without an offset, in microseconds.

### Errors

None.
precedent.why: The later utc_now contract requires a naive UTC microsecond value and declares that the operation has no error outcome, so mark does not choose between the proposed failure behaviors.

topics.topic: Startup behavior when the token file is missing or unreadable
questions: What happens when `token_file` is absent, cannot be opened, or cannot be read: must startup fail, or may the service create a token file?

quotes:
At the start it is opened once; its last component is
   opened without following a link, while the folders above it belong to the installation and are
   resolved as they stand.
judgement.why: P1 already judged the same startup question for an absent, unopenable or unreadable token file, and the relevant passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Startup behavior when the token file path is absent or the file cannot be opened or read
quotes: A file that breaks A5 rule 2 or cannot be read ends the start.
precedent.why: The later read_token contract makes an unreadable token file terminate startup, covering an absent, unopenable or incompletely readable file.
